issue: Run-22 queue item 1: whether the method names a participant reads on the participant surface should be renamed before the study runs
options: (a) keep the frozen names, run the study, rename never or after the study; (b) rename now, re-freeze, re-hash and re-qualify the participant surface before any session; (c) rename only names no participant reads, leaving the participant surface untouched
scientific_consequence: None. The names are labels on methods whose behaviour, dispositions and lineage are unchanged by what they are called. No band, threshold, weight or arithmetic result depends on a name.
instrument_consequence: (b) would invalidate the freeze taken by this run: the participant-package hash, the production-tree manifest hash and the freeze manifest hash all change, and the real-browser participant qualification would have to be re-run against the renamed build.
participant_consequence: This is the whole of the issue. A rename applied MID-SEQUENCE means two participants, or one participant across two assignments, read different words for the same method, which is an uncontrolled variation in the stimulus. Applied BEFORE any session it costs nothing to the study and only costs a re-freeze.
voting_consequence: None. Renaming a label cannot change which modules vote. Voting is derived from the registry and remains exactly {A1.7
blocks_release: The names as frozen at ba5bfaf/the Run-22 release commit. They are recorded in the freeze manifest so the current state is auditable and any later rename is a visible, hashed change rather than a silent edit.
column11: The queue's own condition is 'blocking for a release that RENAMES anything a participant reads'. This release renames nothing a participant reads, so the condition is not met and the release is not blocked. The decision is genuinely the owner's and Run 22 does not make it. THE ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE IT URGENT: the praxis constraint that no participant session may begin before the instrument gates are green. If the owner intends to rename at all, the cheapest and only clean moment is BEFORE the first participant session, because after that a rename is a protocol change and not a cosmetic one.

issue: Run-22 queue item 2: the fixed N for B1.4 Worst-N-of-M has no source in anything this repository holds or cites
options: (a) obtain a source or an owner policy fixing N; (b) leave B1.4 PARAMETER_PROVENANCE_BLOCKED, advisory and non-voting, as a documented post-study limitation
scientific_consequence: B1.4 remains short of SCIENTIFIC_PASS. It is one of the hundred targets and its disposition is truthfully recorded as blocked rather than passed.
instrument_consequence: None while blocked. The module computes and discloses its blocked provenance rather than presenting an unsupported figure as authoritative.
participant_consequence: A participant never meets B1.4 as an authoritative status: it is ADVISORY_ONLY and reaches no governed status.
voting_consequence: None. B1.4 is not in CORE_VOTING_MODULES.
safe_current_state: PARAMETER_PROVENANCE_BLOCKED, ADVISORY_ONLY, non-voting -- verified from the registry and the Run-20 re-audit, not from the narrative.
reason: The safe state is already the blocked one and it is enforced in code, so no unsupported authoritative behaviour can reach a participant. Inventing N is forbidden by the controlling prompt and by this programme's standing rules. Live web is not available in this session, so no external source could be sought; that is recorded as the reason rather than treated as a blocker.

issue: Run-22 queue item 4: empirical validation of the analytical modules is a research programme, not an engineering task
options: (a) scope and run Study A, the offline analytical validation against planted scenario conditions, as the praxis two-study architecture already describes; (b) report the instrument as qualified and the modules as unvalidated
scientific_consequence: Every disposition short of SCIENTIFIC_PASS is short of it for want of a labelled outcome corpus and an expert reference standard. That is a true statement about the state of knowledge, not a defect in the code.
instrument_consequence: None. The instrument is qualified as an instrument; that is what Runs 21 and 22 establish.
participant_consequence: None, PROVIDED the release makes no validated-performance claim. The praxis constraint is explicit that module accuracy must never become a participant-facing claim, and the frozen surface makes no such claim.
safe_current_state: The release definition states in terms that this release qualifies an INSTRUMENT and does not claim validated analytical performance.
reason: Blocking only for a claim this release does not make. Recorded as a standing limitation on the freeze.
